title: Statistical tests; Experimental design and variables
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PR01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; PR03b#t3 term and clue written for the game; PR03b#t2 term and clue written for the game; PR01a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: PR01a#N.2a, PR03b#N.7, PR01a#N.6, PR03b#N.9, PR01a#N.8, PR01a#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Independent variable
items.clue: The one factor the experimenter changes on purpose.

items.label: Null hypothesis
items.clue: States that there is no significant difference between the two means.

items.label: Degrees of freedom
items.clue: For comparing two means: the two sample sizes added together, minus 2.

items.label: Negative control
items.clue: Set-up in which no effect is expected, such as one using a boiled enzyme.

questions.stem: A student places a lamp at different distances from a beaker of pondweed in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution kept at 25 °C, and counts the bubbles of gas released per minute at each distance. Which correctly identifies the variables?

options.text: Independent: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: bubbles per minute; dependent: distance of lamp
Controlled variable: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: temperature of 25 °C; dependent: bubbles per minute

questions.explanation: The lamp distance is what the student deliberately changes (it sets the light intensity), so it is the independent variable; the bubble count is measured to find the effect, so it is the dependent variable. Temperature and hydrogencarbonate concentration are controlled variables.

questions.stem: For 10 quadrats, a student ranks the density of a moss and the soil moisture content, and finds Σd² = 60. The critical value of rₛ for n = 10 at p = 0.05 is 0.648. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: rₛ = 0.64, which is below 0.648, so there is no significant correlation.
rₛ = 0.36, a weak positive correlation that is not significant.
rₛ = 0.64, a positive value, so there is a significant positive correlation.
rₛ = 0.64, which is greater than 0.05, so the correlation is significant.

questions.explanation: rₛ = 1 − (6 × 60) ÷ (10 × 99) = 1 − 360 ÷ 990 = 0.64. Just below the critical value: the correlation could be due to chance.

questions.stem: A student plans to test whether the number of double bonds in a fatty acid affects its melting point, using fatty acids with 0, 1, 2 and 3 double bonds that all have the same chain length. Which statement is an appropriate null hypothesis for this investigation?

options.text: Fatty acids with more double bonds will melt at lower temperatures than those with fewer.
Fatty acids with more double bonds will melt at higher temperatures than those with fewer.
The number of double bonds in a fatty acid has no effect on its melting point.
None of the fatty acids will melt at any of the temperatures used in the investigation.

questions.stem: A student counts the heart rate of Daphnia in pond water (control) and in a caffeine solution, 10 Daphnia in each. - Control: mean 212 beats per minute, SD 18. - Caffeine: mean 231 beats per minute, SD 20. Critical values of t at p = 0.05: 9 degrees of freedom, 2.26; 18, 2.10; 20, 2.09. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: t = 9.75, far above 2.10, so the difference is highly significant.
t = 2.23, above 2.10 for 18 degrees of freedom, so reject the null hypothesis.
t = 2.23, below 2.26 for 9 degrees of freedom, so accept the null hypothesis.
t = 2.23, above 2.10, which proves caffeine raises the heart rate of every Daphnia.

questions.stem: A filter-paper disc soaked in catalase solution sinks in hydrogen peroxide and rises when enough oxygen has formed on it. In 1% hydrogen peroxide the disc took 50 s to rise; in 2% it took 20 s. Which statement about the reaction rate is correct?

options.text: Rate is proportional to 1/time, so the rate at 2% (0.05 s⁻¹) is 2.5 times the rate at 1% (0.02 s⁻¹).
The rate at 1% is 50 and at 2% is 20, so the rate fell when the concentration was doubled.
Doubling the concentration doubles the rate, so the rate at 2% is 0.04 s⁻¹, twice that at 1%.
The rate cannot be found, because the volume of oxygen produced was not measured in either trial.

questions.stem: Ecologists want to test the hypothesis that two limpet species compete for algae on a shore. Which approach tests the hypothesis by experiment rather than by observation?

options.text: Removing one limpet species from marked plots and recording the growth of the other over a year.
Recording the abundance of both limpet species in quadrats placed at random positions along the shore.
Measuring the shell sizes of both limpet species in laboratory tanks of seawater collected from the shore.
Applying a chi-squared test to records of where each species occurred in past shore surveys.
